degenerateAxes.cpm: Central Package Management is not a separate package manager. It is `ManagePackageVersionsCentrally=true` layered on top of PackageReference: same client, same restore, same lock file, versions hoisted to Directory.Packages.props.

prose.note: README.md must be able to state OpenTelemetry's and Coverlet's own floors, which are netstandard2.0 -- a true sentence naming a foreign framework. The allowance is scoped to ONE file and ONE version so the blast radius is a single document. Widening the rule instead would silently un-catch the bug it was written for.

languageFixture.note: The domain layer is byte-identical across all 24 branches of this family, so any tool-output difference is attributable to the cell variables and nothing else.

expectations.note: A dark tool is a data point, not a failure. But a family in which NOTHING fires cannot distinguish 'correctly detected nothing' from 'the scan never ran', which is why the source-level tools below are the built-in negative control.

tools.reason: Python tokeniser. Class B: own parser, never loads a compiler, so the TFM is irrelevant to it.

Node, tree-sitter C# grammar. Class B, and the sheet's declaration ('C# language-version independent - source similarity, not tied to compiler') is correct. MEASURED, not assumed: @dodona/dolos 2.9.3 fails to install on this host because @dodona/dolos-parsers 1.4.1 needs node-gyp native compilation, which fails under node 22.22.2. That is exit 4 (absent from this host), not exit 3 (cannot run on this family) -- collapsing the two would let a missing binary masquerade as a .NET Framework result.
Python, tree-sitter C# grammar. Class B.

Standalone binary, absent from this host. Class B when present. NOTE: the sheet declares 'C# 12+', which inverts the hazard -- a tree-sitter grammar has no language floor, only a construct set, so the risk runs toward NEWER syntax.
Standalone Go binary, absent from this host. Class C: reads manifests/lockfiles.
Python, reads git only. Class C: never touches the source language.
stdlib git. Class C. Counts Co-authored-by trailers, not just the author field -- the TypeScript corpus's ownership metric was wrong, not missing, for exactly this reason.
Class C: reads Cobertura/OpenCover XML. Coverlet now produces one on this branch, so diff-cover has something to read wherever it is installed.
The sheet says 'Roslyn', which is a compiler platform, not a package. Resolved here to SonarAnalyzer.CSharp 9.32.0.97167 (rule S3776 is cognitive complexity), referenced as an analyzer package.
The sheet says 'roslyn sast', also not a package. Resolved here to SecurityCodeScan.VS2019 5.6.7 + Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers 8.0.0, referenced as analyzer packages.

PROPOSED REPAIR, not in the source sheet. The sheet assigns Data Flow to Stryker.NET, a mutation tester that computes no def-use chains. AnalyzeDataFlow is a real Roslyn API that ships in the SDK and yields genuine def/use sets.
The planted pins are PackageReference items, so `dotnet list package --vulnerable` reads them directly. `--no-restore` is left out: an 8.0 SDK rejects it and prints its help text instead of a report.

coverlet.collector 6.0.0 is referenced by the test project, with its version in Directory.Packages.props, so `dotnet test --collect` produces Cobertura XML. The test host rolls forward to the nearest newer runtime when this one is not installed.
altcover.global 8.8.173 is pinned in .config/dotnet-tools.json. It instruments the built test output in place, so no project file names it.

MiniCover 3.10.0 declares .NET SDK 8.0/9.0/10.0 only -- verified against its own MiniCover.csproj (<TargetFrameworks>net10.0;net9.0;net8.0</TargetFrameworks>). It is the alternative for 22 metrics and cannot reach any .NET Framework target.

Stryker.NET 4.0.0 runs as the host's installed `dotnet stryker` and mutates this family: it restores the solution, mutates the library, runs the tests against each mutant and writes a mutation report. It is deliberately absent from .config/dotnet-tools.json: an entry there makes `dotnet stryker` demand `dotnet tool restore` and stop, instead of running the installed tool. Also: the sheet makes it primary for 16 Data Flow metrics, which it cannot compute -- see roslyn-dataflow.

OpenTelemetry 1.19.1 and its OTLP exporter are restored into the test project, and TracingSetup.cs in the test project wraps the run in a trace. Spans leave the process only when a collector is named; with none the export is dropped, which would be a structurally zero result. Note separately that tracing is not path coverage.

NOT A TOOL. The only package of this name anywhere is PyPI `unilyze` 0.2.1, 'Get detailed unicode information about characters and text', last released 2020-07-23. Not on npm. It has no .NET surface of any kind. The source sheet assigns it as the alternative for 34 of the 103 metrics and declares '.NET 8-10, C# 8-14' for it, which is a fabricated capability claim. This runner exits 3 and says so, so the hole is visible rather than invisible.

plantedFixtures.taintSources: every public parameter -- a library does not control its callers, so an engine that only recognises argv, environment or a request object misses all four flows
